function.name: search_holy_books
function.description: Search content, chapters or authors of holy books. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

book.description: The name of the holy book.

chapter.description: The chapter number, if relevant. Default: 3

content.description: Specific content to look for, if relevant.

message.content:
A **holy book** (also called a sacred text) is a written work that is considered divinely inspired, authoritative, and central to the beliefs, practices, and moral teachings of a particular religion or spiritual tradition. These texts are often regarded as the word of God, a divine revelation, or the culmination of spiritual wisdom. Key characteristics include:

| Feature | Typical Description |
|---------|---------------------|
| **Divine Origin** | Believed to be revealed by a deity, angel, or other supernatural source. |
| **Authority** | Provides guidance on theology, law, ethics, rituals, and cosmology. |
| **Centrality** | Forms the core of religious identity and community life. |
| **Preservation** | Transmitted through generations via oral tradition, manuscripts, and later printed editions. |
| **Interpretation** | Subject to exegesis, commentaries, and scholarly debate. |

Examples of holy books across world religions:

| Religion | Holy Book(s) | Notes |
|----------|--------------|-------|
| Christianity | *Bible* (Old & New Testaments) | Written over centuries; central to Christian faith. |
| Islam | *Qur’an* | Considered the literal word of God (Allah). |
| Judaism | *Tanakh* (Hebrew Bible) | Includes Torah, Prophets, Writings. |
| Hinduism | *Vedas*, *Upanishads*, *Bhagavad Gita* | Sacred scriptures with diverse origins. |
| Buddhism | *Tripitaka*, *Sutra* collections | Teachings of Buddha and his disciples. |
| Sikhism | *Guru Granth Sahib* | Guru’s hymns and writings. |
| Jainism | *Agamas* | Canonical texts of Jain philosophy. |
| Baháʼí Faith | *Kitáb-i-Aqdas*, *Kitáb-i-Íqán* | Writings of Bahá’u’lláh. |

While each tradition has its own criteria for what constitutes a holy book, common themes include divine inspiration, moral authority, and a role in shaping communal identity and practice.
